citations.narrative:
It has been over a year since the last documented annual review of the contingency plan, which occurred on 01 March
2025. Reviewing the plan regularly (on at least an annual basis) ensures the facility has made assessments for any
needed changes to better prepare for emergencies. The facility shall develop and document an appropriate contingency
plan, as well as maintain review documentation and have it available for APHIS inspections.
To be corrected by 17 August 2026.

Dry food for birds on hand (emu and pheasants) is being stored in open and unopened bags stacked directly on the floor
and tucked against the walls in the storage shed. The plywood floor has a layer of dried food pellets, dirt and discarded
empty food bags covering it. Supplies of food, including food supplements, bedding, and substrate must be stored in a
manner that protects against deterioration, spoilage, contamination, and vermin infestation. The supplies must be stored
off the floor and away from the walls, to allow cleaning underneath and around the supplies.
To be corrected by 17 August 2026.

citations.desc: Environment enhancement to promote psychological well-being.
citations.narrative:
At the time of inspection, the licensee had pheasants and emu on exhibit and a written avian environment enhancement
plan was not available for review. Lack of an environment enhancement plan covering all bird species and approved by
the Attending Veterinarian (AV) does not ensure that environmental and social needs are properly being provided. The
plan must be developed to address the social, environmental and special considerations for all birds at the facility and
approved by the AV.
To be corrected by 15 September 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
